001package io.jstach.rainbowgum;
002
003import java.text.MessageFormat;
004import java.util.Arrays;
005import java.util.IdentityHashMap;
006import java.util.Locale;
007
008import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
009
010import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.CaseChanging;

013/**
014 * Formats a LogEvent message.
015 *
016 * @apiNote This is sealed at the moment and maybe unsealed in the future so exhaustive
017 * pattern matching should not be done.
018 */
019@CaseChanging
020public sealed interface LogMessageFormatter {
021
022        /**
023         * Formats and appends the results.
024         * @param builder output.
025         * @param message message usually with formatting delimiters for replacement.
026         * @param arg1 to use for replacement.
027         */
028        void format(StringBuilder builder, String message, @Nullable Object arg1);
029
030        /**
031         * Formats and appends the results.
032         * @param builder output.
033         * @param message message usually with formatting delimiters for replacement.
034         * @param arg1 to use for replacement.
035         * @param arg2 to use for replacement.
036         */
037        void format(StringBuilder builder, String message, @Nullable Object arg1, @Nullable Object arg2);
038
039        /**
040         * Formats and appends the result.
041         * @param builder output.
042         * @param message message usually with formatting delimiters for replacement.
043         * @param args array of args.
044         */
045        default void formatArray(StringBuilder builder, String message, @Nullable Object[] args) {
046                formatArray(builder, message, args, args.length);
047        }
048
049        /**
050         * Formats and appends the result.
051         * @param builder output.
052         * @param message message usually with formatting delimiters for replacement.
053         * @param args array of args.
054         * @param length of args array which will be used even if args is larger.
055         */
056        void formatArray(StringBuilder builder, String message, @Nullable Object[] args, int length);
057
058        /**
059         * The java.util.logging, System.Logger and JBoss Logging MessageFormat style as
060         * configured by {@value LogProperties#MESSAGE_FORMAT_STYLE_PROPERTY}.
061         * @param properties usually the properties of the current Rainbow Gum's config.
062         * @return {@link StandardMessageFormatter#JUL} when the property has its default
063         * value, otherwise a formatter that follows it.
064         * @throws LogProperty.ValidationException if the property has an invalid value.
065         */
066        public static LogMessageFormatter ofJUL(LogProperties properties) {
067                return MessageFormatStyle.of(properties).formatter();
068        }
069
070        /**
071         * Built-in message formatters.
072         */
073        @CaseChanging
074        public enum StandardMessageFormatter implements LogMessageFormatter {
075
076                /**
077                 * SLF4J format style where "<code>{}</code>" is replaced with the parameters. The
078                 * implementation largely comes from the SLF4J but optimized for StringBuilder.
079                 */
080                SLF4J() {
081                        @Override
082                        public void format(StringBuilder builder, String message, @Nullable Object arg1) {
083                                SLF4JMessageFormatter.format(builder, message, arg1);
084                        }
085
086                        @Override
087                        public void format(StringBuilder builder, String message, @Nullable Object arg1, @Nullable Object arg2) {
088                                SLF4JMessageFormatter.format(builder, message, arg1, arg2);
089                        }
090
091                        @Override
092                        public void formatArray(StringBuilder builder, String message, @Nullable Object[] args, int length) {
093                                SLF4JMessageFormatter.format(builder, message, args, length);
094                        }
095                },
096                /**
097                 * java.util.logging MessageFormat style following the rules of the JDK's
098                 * <code>java.util.logging.Formatter.formatMessage</code>: {@link MessageFormat}
099                 * is used only when there are arguments and the message has an argument index
100                 * such as <code>{0}</code>, otherwise the message is logged as is. A
101                 * {@link Throwable} argument is formatted like any other argument.
102                 * @see LogMessageFormatter#ofJUL(LogProperties)
103                 */
104                JUL() {
105
106                        @Override
107                        public void format(StringBuilder builder, String message, @Nullable Object arg1) {
108                                if (MessageFormatStyle.hasArgumentIndex(message)) {
109                                        Log4j2MessageFormatter.INSTANCE.format(builder, message, arg1);
110                                }
111                                else {
112                                        builder.append(message);
113                                }
114                        }
115
116                        @Override
117                        public void format(StringBuilder builder, String message, @Nullable Object arg1, @Nullable Object arg2) {
118                                if (MessageFormatStyle.hasArgumentIndex(message)) {
119                                        Log4j2MessageFormatter.INSTANCE.format(builder, message, arg1, arg2);
120                                }
121                                else {
122                                        builder.append(message);
123                                }
124                        }
125
126                        @Override
127                        public void formatArray(StringBuilder builder, String message, @Nullable Object[] args, int length) {
128                                if (MessageFormatStyle.hasArgumentIndex(message)) {
129                                        Log4j2MessageFormatter.INSTANCE.formatArray(builder, message, args, length);
130                                }
131                                else {
132                                        builder.append(message);
133                                }
134                        }
135
136                }
137
138        }
139
140}
141
142/*
143 * Values of LogProperties.MESSAGE_FORMAT_STYLE_PROPERTY, named after the implementation
144 * whose System.Logger formats the same way.
145 */
146enum MessageFormatStyle {
147
148        /*
149         * MessageFormat only when there is an argument index, a Throwable argument is only an
150         * argument. JBoss LogManager does the same.
151         */
152        @EnumAlias({ "default", "jboss" })
153        JDK,
154        /*
155         * MessageFormat whenever there are arguments, a trailing Throwable argument is also
156         * the event's throwable. SLF4J's System.Logger adapter, and so Logback, does the
157         * same.
158         */
159        @EnumAlias("logback")
160        LOG4J2;
161
162        static MessageFormatStyle parse(String value) {
163                String v = value.strip().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
164                return switch (v) {
165                        case "DEFAULT", "JBOSS" -> JDK;
166                        case "LOGBACK" -> LOG4J2;
167                        default -> LogProperty.enumValue(MessageFormatStyle.class, value, "default", "jboss", "logback");
168                };
169        }
170
171        static MessageFormatStyle of(LogProperties properties) {
172                var validator = LogProperty.Validator.of(LogMessageFormatter.class);
173                var style = properties.forKey(LogProperties.MESSAGE_FORMAT_STYLE_PROPERTY)
174                        .ofString()
175                        .map(MessageFormatStyle::parse)
176                        .or(JDK)
177                        .validateIfError(validator);
178                validator.validate();
179                return style.value();
180        }
181
182        LogMessageFormatter formatter() {
183                return switch (this) {
184                        case JDK -> LogMessageFormatter.StandardMessageFormatter.JUL;
185                        case LOG4J2 -> Log4j2MessageFormatter.INSTANCE;
186                };
187        }
188
189        /*
190         * Whether a trailing Throwable argument is also the event's throwable.
191         */
192        static boolean throwableAlsoArgument(LogMessageFormatter messageFormatter) {
193                return messageFormatter == Log4j2MessageFormatter.INSTANCE;
194        }
195
196        /*
197         * The same check java.util.logging.Formatter.formatMessage does: a '{' followed by a
198         * digit. Without one, MessageFormat has nothing to replace and would only strip
199         * apostrophes, which it treats as quotes.
200         */
201        static boolean hasArgumentIndex(String message) {
202                int fence = message.length() - 1;
203                int index = message.indexOf('{');
204                while (index >= 0 && index < fence) {
205                        char c = message.charAt(index + 1);
206                        if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') {
207                                return true;
208                        }
209                        index = message.indexOf('{', index + 1);
210                }
211                return false;
212        }
213
214}
215
216/*
217 * MessageFormatStyle.LOG4J2: MessageFormat whenever there are arguments. The JDK style
218 * uses it when the message has an argument index.
219 */
220enum Log4j2MessageFormatter implements LogMessageFormatter {
221
222        INSTANCE;
223
224        @Override
225        public void format(StringBuilder builder, String message, @Nullable Object arg1) {
226                try {
227                        String result = MessageFormat.format(message, arg1);
228                        builder.append(result);
229                }
230                catch (Throwable e) {
231                        formatBadPattern(builder, message, e);
232                }
233        }
234
235        @Override
236        public void format(StringBuilder builder, String message, @Nullable Object arg1, @Nullable Object arg2) {
237                try {
238                        String result = MessageFormat.format(message, arg1, arg2);
239                        builder.append(result);
240                }
241                catch (Throwable e) {
242                        formatBadPattern(builder, message, e);
243                }
244        }
245
246        @Override
247        public void formatArray(StringBuilder builder, String message, @Nullable Object[] args, int length) {
248                if (length == 0) {
249                        builder.append(message);
250                        return;
251                }
252                @Nullable Object[] used = length == args.length ? args : Arrays.copyOf(args, length);
253                try {
254                        String result = MessageFormat.format(message, used);
255                        builder.append(result);
256                }
257                catch (Throwable e) {
258                        formatBadPattern(builder, message, e);
259                }
260        }
261
262        /*
263         * A malformed pattern or an argument whose toString() throws must not lose the event
264         * or throw to the caller. The JDK logs the raw pattern without saying why, Log4j2 and
265         * JBoss LogManager drop the event, and Logback through SLF4J's adapter throws to the
266         * caller. We log the raw pattern and the reason, much like the SLF4J style's
267         * "[FAILED toString()]", rather than raising an alert: the message may come from
268         * outside, and an alert per bad message would let a caller make the service look
269         * unhealthy. An Error from toString(), such as the StackOverflowError of a recursive
270         * one, is handled the same way; only an error that leaves the JVM unusable is
271         * rethrown. The reason is the exception's message, or its class name when it has
272         * none.
273         */
274        private static void formatBadPattern(StringBuilder builder, String message, Throwable e) {
275                if (e instanceof VirtualMachineError fatal && !(e instanceof StackOverflowError)) {
276                        throw fatal;
277                }
278                builder.append(message).append(" [MessageFormat failed: ").append(reason(e)).append("]");
279        }
280
281        /*
282         * getMessage() can be overridden, so it is guarded like toString().
283         */
284        private static String reason(Throwable e) {
285                try {
286                        String reason = e.getMessage();
287                        if (reason != null) {
288                                return reason;
289                        }
290                }
291                catch (Throwable ignored) {
292                        // fall back to the class name
293                }
294                return e.getClass().getName();
295        }
296
297}
298
299final class SLF4JMessageFormatter {
300
301        private static final char DELIM_START = '{';
302
303        private static final String DELIM_STR = "{}";
304
305        private static final char ESCAPE_CHAR = '\\';
306
307        private SLF4JMessageFormatter() {
308        }
309
310        public static void format(final StringBuilder sbuf, final @Nullable String messagePattern,
311                        final @Nullable Object arg1) {
312                format(sbuf, messagePattern, arg1, null, null, 1);
313        }
314
315        public static void format(final StringBuilder sbuf, final @Nullable String messagePattern,
316                        final @Nullable Object arg1, final @Nullable Object arg2) {
317                format(sbuf, messagePattern, arg1, arg2, null, 2);
318        }
319
320        public static void format(final StringBuilder sbuf, final @Nullable String messagePattern,
321                        final @Nullable Object @Nullable [] args, int length) {
322                if (args == null || length == 0) {
323                        format(sbuf, messagePattern, null, null, null, 0);
324                        return;
325                }
326                else if (length == 1) {
327                        format(sbuf, messagePattern, args[0], null, null, 1);
328                        return;
329                }
330                else if (length == 2) {
331                        format(sbuf, messagePattern, args[0], args[1], null, 2);
332                        return;
333                }
334                else {
335                        format(sbuf, messagePattern, null, null, args, length);
336                }
337        }
338
339        private static void format(final StringBuilder sbuf, //
340                        final @Nullable String messagePattern, //
341                        final @Nullable Object arg1, //
342                        final @Nullable Object arg2, //
343                        final @Nullable Object @Nullable [] args, //
344                        final int argCount) {
345
346                if (messagePattern == null) {
347                        return;
348                }
349
350                if (argCount == 0) {
351                        sbuf.append(messagePattern);
352                        return;
353                }
354
355                int i = 0;
356                int j;
357                int L;
358                for (L = 0; L < argCount; L++) {
359
360                        j = messagePattern.indexOf(DELIM_STR, i);
361
362                        if (j == -1) {
363                                // no more variables
364                                if (i == 0) { // this is a simple string
365                                        sbuf.append(messagePattern);
366                                        return;
367                                }
368                                else { // add the tail string which contains no variables and return
369                                                // the result.
370                                        sbuf.append(messagePattern, i, messagePattern.length());
371                                        return;
372                                }
373                        }
374                        else {
375                                if (isEscapedDelimeter(messagePattern, j)) {
376                                        if (!isDoubleEscaped(messagePattern, j)) {
377                                                L--; // DELIM_START was escaped, thus should not be incremented
378                                                sbuf.append(messagePattern, i, j - 1);
379                                                sbuf.append(DELIM_START);
380                                                i = j + 1;
381                                        }
382                                        else {
383                                                // The escape character preceding the delimiter start is
384                                                // itself escaped: "abc x:\\{}"
385                                                // we have to consume one backward slash
386                                                sbuf.append(messagePattern, i, j - 1);
387                                                Object arg = resolveArg(L, arg1, arg2, args, argCount);
388                                                deeplyAppendParameter(sbuf, arg, null);
389                                                i = j + 2;
390                                        }
391                                }
392                                else {
393                                        // normal case
394                                        sbuf.append(messagePattern, i, j);
395                                        Object arg = resolveArg(L, arg1, arg2, args, argCount);
396                                        deeplyAppendParameter(sbuf, arg, null);
397                                        i = j + 2;
398                                }
399                        }
400                }
401                // append the characters following the last {} pair.
402                sbuf.append(messagePattern, i, messagePattern.length());
403        }
404
405        private static @Nullable Object resolveArg(int i, @Nullable Object arg1, @Nullable Object arg2,
406                        @Nullable Object @Nullable [] args, int argCount) {
407                if (i >= argCount || argCount == 0) {
408                        throw new IndexOutOfBoundsException(i);
409                }
410                if (argCount > 2) {
411                        if (args == null) {
412                                throw new IndexOutOfBoundsException(i);
413                        }
414                        return args[i];
415                }
416                else if (i == 0) {
417                        return arg1;
418                }
419                else if (i == 1) {
420                        return arg2;
421                }
422                throw new IndexOutOfBoundsException(i);
423        }
424
425        final static boolean isEscapedDelimeter(String messagePattern, int delimeterStartIndex) {
426
427                if (delimeterStartIndex == 0) {
428                        return false;
429                }
430                char potentialEscape = messagePattern.charAt(delimeterStartIndex - 1);
431                if (potentialEscape == ESCAPE_CHAR) {
432                        return true;
433                }
434                else {
435                        return false;
436                }
437        }
438
439        final static boolean isDoubleEscaped(String messagePattern, int delimeterStartIndex) {
440                if (delimeterStartIndex >= 2 && messagePattern.charAt(delimeterStartIndex - 2) == ESCAPE_CHAR) {
441                        return true;
442                }
443                else {
444                        return false;
445                }
446        }
447
448        /*
449         * The below is adapted code from SLF4J
450         */
451        // special treatment of array values was suggested by 'lizongbo'
452        private static void deeplyAppendParameter(StringBuilder sbuf, @Nullable Object o,
453                        @Nullable IdentityHashMap<@Nullable Object[], @Nullable Object> seenMap) {
454                if (o == null) {
455                        sbuf.append("null");
456                        return;
457                }
458                if (!o.getClass().isArray()) {
459                        safeObjectAppend(sbuf, o);
460                }
461                else {
462                        // check for primitive array types because they
463                        // unfortunately cannot be cast to Object[]
464                        if (o instanceof boolean[] array) {
465                                booleanArrayAppend(sbuf, array);
466                        }
467                        else if (o instanceof byte[] array) {
468                                byteArrayAppend(sbuf, array);
469                        }
470                        else if (o instanceof char[] array) {
471                                charArrayAppend(sbuf, array);
472                        }
473                        else if (o instanceof short[] array) {
474                                shortArrayAppend(sbuf, array);
475                        }
476                        else if (o instanceof int[] array) {
477                                intArrayAppend(sbuf, array);
478                        }
479                        else if (o instanceof long[] array) {
480                                longArrayAppend(sbuf, array);
481                        }
482                        else if (o instanceof float[] array) {
483                                floatArrayAppend(sbuf, array);
484                        }
485                        else if (o instanceof double[] array) {
486                                doubleArrayAppend(sbuf, array);
487                        }
488                        else {
489                                if (seenMap == null) {
490                                        seenMap = new IdentityHashMap<>();
491                                }
492                                objectArrayAppend(sbuf, (@Nullable Object[]) o, seenMap);
493                        }
494                }
495        }
496
497        private static void safeObjectAppend(StringBuilder sbuf, Object o) {
498                try {
499                        String oAsString = o.toString();
500                        sbuf.append(oAsString);
501                }
502                catch (Throwable t) {
503                        sbuf.append("[FAILED toString()]");
504                }
505
506        }
507
508        private static void objectArrayAppend(StringBuilder sbuf, @Nullable Object[] a,
509                        IdentityHashMap<@Nullable Object[], @Nullable Object> seenMap) {
510                sbuf.append('[');
511                if (!seenMap.containsKey(a)) {
512                        seenMap.put(a, null);
513                        final int len = a.length;
514                        for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
515                                deeplyAppendParameter(sbuf, a[i], seenMap);
516                                if (i != len - 1)
517                                        sbuf.append(", ");
518                        }
519                        // allow repeats in siblings
520                        seenMap.remove(a);
521                }
522                else {
523                        sbuf.append("...");
524                }
525                sbuf.append(']');
526        }
527
528        private static void booleanArrayAppend(StringBuilder sbuf, boolean[] a) {
529                sbuf.append('[');
530                final int len = a.length;
531                for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
532                        sbuf.append(a[i]);
533                        if (i != len - 1)
534                                sbuf.append(", ");
535                }
536                sbuf.append(']');
537        }
538
539        private static void byteArrayAppend(StringBuilder sbuf, byte[] a) {
540                sbuf.append('[');
541                final int len = a.length;
542                for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
543                        sbuf.append(a[i]);
544                        if (i != len - 1)
545                                sbuf.append(", ");
546                }
547                sbuf.append(']');
548        }
549
550        private static void charArrayAppend(StringBuilder sbuf, char[] a) {
551                sbuf.append('[');
552                final int len = a.length;
553                for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
554                        sbuf.append(a[i]);
555                        if (i != len - 1)
556                                sbuf.append(", ");
557                }
558                sbuf.append(']');
559        }
560
561        private static void shortArrayAppend(StringBuilder sbuf, short[] a) {
562                sbuf.append('[');
563                final int len = a.length;
564                for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
565                        sbuf.append(a[i]);
566                        if (i != len - 1)
567                                sbuf.append(", ");
568                }
569                sbuf.append(']');
570        }
571
572        private static void intArrayAppend(StringBuilder sbuf, int[] a) {
573                sbuf.append('[');
574                final int len = a.length;
575                for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
576                        sbuf.append(a[i]);
577                        if (i != len - 1)
578                                sbuf.append(", ");
579                }
580                sbuf.append(']');
581        }
582
583        private static void longArrayAppend(StringBuilder sbuf, long[] a) {
584                sbuf.append('[');
585                final int len = a.length;
586                for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
587                        sbuf.append(a[i]);
588                        if (i != len - 1)
589                                sbuf.append(", ");
590                }
591                sbuf.append(']');
592        }
593
594        private static void floatArrayAppend(StringBuilder sbuf, float[] a) {
595                sbuf.append('[');
596                final int len = a.length;
597                for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
598                        sbuf.append(a[i]);
599                        if (i != len - 1)
600                                sbuf.append(", ");
601                }
602                sbuf.append(']');
603        }
604
605        private static void doubleArrayAppend(StringBuilder sbuf, double[] a) {
606                sbuf.append('[');
607                final int len = a.length;
608                for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {
609                        sbuf.append(a[i]);
610                        if (i != len - 1)
611                                sbuf.append(", ");
612                }
613                sbuf.append(']');
614        }
